reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode through Nov 6: SPX -5.96% from its 120-day high, -3.94% below its 50-day but +0.71% above its 200-day; SMH $463.96 sits below Zone 2 ($470–505) and NVDA $186.64 between zones; VIX 25.64 is rolling over from a 28.18 five-day high but still above the 25 stand-down line; HY OAS 3.48 is calm and the mechanical tally is 3 of 4 with zone occupancy the missing leg.
reaction.invalidation: A Zone 2 print that fails — SMH closing back below $470 within two sessions of entering it — or HY OAS above 4% proves the Watch stance wrong and voids the ladder. Conversely, a sustained SPX close above its 50-day at 7,679.45 with VIX under 25 would prove the correction over and flip the stance toward Add.

ladder.response: Stay Watch — no Probe. The washout extends; the next decision point is a fresh Zone 2 print, not a lower catch.
Treat as the trap case: sell-the-rally zone, not a breakout. Do not chase; any Probe waits for a close back above the failure zone with VIX under 25.
ladder.trigger: SPX rallies into the failure zone $7,750–7,820, or SMH into $580–600, without a Zone 2 print first

ladder.response: Stand down fully — cancel all Probe plans. Credit cracking or vol re-spiking voids the rotation read and the ladder.
ladder.trigger: VIX closes back above 28.18 (5-day high) or HY OAS closes above 4%

ladder.response: Arm the Tranche A probe per the ladder at starter sizing; confirm on the next close before adding anything.
ladder.trigger: SMH closes inside Zone 2 ($470–505) or NVDA inside $175–185, with VIX closing below 25 and the tally at 4 of 4

reaction.trapRisk: Friday's +1.62% QQQ and +3.91% NVDA bounce came with no zone print and VIX still above 25 — the classic first-bounce setup. Entries that chase the bounce get trapped if the second low breaks the 200-day at 7,325.05. No chasing: wait for the failure-zone retest verdict (SPX $7,750–7,820) or a Zone 2 print with VIX under 25 before any Probe.

strategyPosture: Watch. Friday was the washout and the first bounce, not a confirmation: no name printed inside a buy zone, VIX is still above 25, and the tally is 3 of 4 with zone occupancy missing. Cash stays king until a Zone 2 print plus VIX under 25 arms the ladder.

themes.counterRead: Index-level calm is masking real weakness concentrated in the handful of names that dominate by weight. The rotation read holds only while credit stays loose — if lending standards flip, rotation becomes rollover fast, and the divergence gap itself is the thing to track.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag 7 averages -17.44% from 52-week highs against SPX -5.9%, an 11.54-point divergence gap, with GOOGL the weakest at -30.3% and AAPL the strongest at -3.7%. But the index itself is only -5.96% off its 120-day high and still +0.71% above its 200-day, bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7% (far below the ~40% stress threshold), and non-AI leaders are positive over one month — NXT +19.14%, MA +13.33%, TMDX +11.52%.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover — Mag 7 collapse vs index calm
themes.narrative: The Mag 7 collapse reads as a broad market rollover — the names that dominate the index by weight are down hard, so the index itself must be next.
themes.watchFor: Mag 7 vs SPX divergence gap widening past 15 points, or lending standards moving out of the LOOSE zone.

themes.counterRead: Revenue recovery is confirmed, not forecast — but the market is derating multiples, and a multiple derate can run further than the fundamentals justify before it turns. The setup is real only if the revenue holds through the next prints; the opportunity is in names where the business is building while the price falls, not in catching the whole complex at once.
themes.dataAnchor: NVDA is -18.13% over one month and -23.3% from its peak while revenue is growing 61.4% YoY (RECOVERY inflection, RSI 30.8, conviction score 83). AVGO is -40.7% from its high with revenue +55% YoY, 67.8% gross margin and a 42.1% FCF margin. DDOG is -40.5% from its high with revenue +27.7% and 80% gross margin; LRCX is -54.3% from its high with revenue +131.3% YoY. Across the board, 35 dislocations are flagged, most SENTIMENT_DRIVEN with RSI in the 24–40 oversold band — oversold, not fundamentally broken.
themes.label: AI infrastructure: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The AI buildout is broken — semis and AI infrastructure names are in freefall, so the fundamentals must be cracking with them.
themes.watchFor: A Zone 2 print — NVDA closing inside $175–185 or SMH closing inside $470–505 — confirms the dislocation is buyable; without it, the data-ahead read stays research, not action.

themes.counterRead: The bounce is real buying, not a dead-cat drift — +23% in a day on OKLO is a washout signature, and VST carries $1.17M of insider buying at the trough. If the bounce holds into next week with a second day of strength, the washout low is in play; if it fades, Friday was the trap's first leg.
themes.dataAnchor: OKLO jumped +23.18% Friday, SMR +15.56%, VST +10.42% — the sharpest single-day moves in the tape. But the one-month damage is still deep: OKLO -31.59%, SMR -31.01%, VST -20.17% over one month, VST -36.6% from its 52-week high, and VST's revenue inflection is flagged DETERIORATING even as its conviction score sits at 80 on a 2.4x P/S. One day of buying does not repair a month of selling.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power: Friday's snapback vs a month of damage
themes.narrative: Friday's snapback means the nuclear / AI-power washout is over — the power names bottomed and the bounce is the turn.
themes.watchFor: OKLO or SMR giving back more than half of Friday's gains (+23.18% / +15.56%) voids the bottom read.

themes.counterRead: Credit is a lagging confirmer, not a leading all-clear: HY OAS at 3.48 can gap if a second AI borrower cracks or the Dec 8–9 FOMC surprises. The calm is the condition that lets a bottom hold when it forms — it is not itself the bottom.
themes.dataAnchor: HY OAS is 3.48 and flagged calm, not cracking; bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7%; the 2s10s curve is +0.38 (positively sloped), the 10-year is 4.84% with a 2.61% real yield, and the Fed funds rate is 3.88%. The equity drawdown is a growth-and-multiple repricing, not a funding seizure — credit has not confirmed the tape.
themes.label: Credit calm while equities stress
themes.narrative: An equity washout this sharp — QQQ -12.05% in a month, VIX +66.39% in a month — means a credit event is coming; the funding channel must be cracking.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4% — that print voids the credit-calm read and flips the episode to regime break.

themes.counterRead: A washout week and a confirmation day are different things: SMH is -11.2% over five days and VIX spiked to a 28.18 five-day high before rolling over. Friday's bounce is the setup for the second-low test, not the test's result.
themes.dataAnchor: Friday was broad and strong: RKLB +16.48%, TSLT +8.31%, ASTS +7.58%, PWR +6.55%, CCJ +5.05%. But the episode state has not confirmed: SPX is still -3.94% below its 50-day, SMH $463.96 sits below Zone 2 ($470–505), NVDA $186.64 sits between zones, VIX 25.64 is still above the 25 stand-down line, and the mechanical tally is 3 of 4 with zone occupancy — the buy-zone leg — unconfirmed. The volume climax (SMH 1.53x average volume, close in 38% of range) and VIX rollover from 28.18 are real, but they are two of four legs.
themes.label: Friday's bounce: washout, not confirmation
themes.narrative: Friday's bounce is the bottom — QQQ +1.62%, NVDA +3.91%, TQQQ +4.09% in a day means the washout is done.
themes.watchFor: Whether Friday's bounce holds or fails into the second-low test — a close below the 200-day at 7,325.05 says the bounce failed.

watchFor: SMH daily close inside Zone 2 ($470–505) or NVDA close inside $175–185 — the zone print that arms Tranche A.
VIX daily close below 25 — lifts the stand-down; a close back above 28.18 (5-day high) re-arms it.
SPX weekly close vs its 200-day at 7,325.05 — holding above keeps the correction contained; breaking below opens the next leg down.
HY OAS above 4% — credit cracking voids the rotation read and the ladder.
FOMC decision Dec 8–9 — the next dated macro catalyst; a hawkish surprise reprices the 10-year (4.84%) and the curve.
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds on the second-low test near the 200-day — SPX closed 7,376.86, just +0.71% above its 200-day at 7,325.05. If the second low holds with volume and the tally rebuilds to 4 of 4, the wave builds into the AI complex (NVDA, AVGO, DDOG) where revenue is recovering into oversold prices; if the 200-day breaks, the wave builds down with the ladder still unarmed.
